problem: Traditional single-agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems struggle when handling diverse and heterogeneous data sources such as relational, document-based, and graph-based databases, leading to performance bottlenecks, token inefficiencies, and reduced query accuracy (p.2, p.9).
methodology: The paper proposes a Multi-Agent RAG system divided into three primary phases: query generation by specialized agents (e.g., MySQL, MongoDB, Neo4j agents) using database schemas and few-shot prompts, query execution within a centralized environment utilizing appropriate database drivers, and response synthesis by a central generative agent (p.9-10, p.13).
key_findings: Delegating tasks to specialized agents within a modular architecture improves query efficiency, reduces token overhead, and enhances response accuracy across complex, heterogeneous data environments (p.2, p.9).
title: A COLLABORATIVE MULTI-AGENT APPROACH TO RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTED GENERATION ACROSS DIVERSE DATA SOURCES
